title: Design: A/R Collection at 1440 px in light theme shows every column
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location column shows.
  • Have a customer, customer A, with a long name (more than 40 characters) and open documents at both locations on today's date, including a credit memo.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with every group expanded (Expand all).
  • Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the title row.
  2. Look at where the filter row sits, and compare with Sales By Customer.
  3. Read the column headings left to right, letter for letter, capitals included.
  4. Look for a sideways scroll bar under the table.
  5. Look at customer A's rows: the name and Transaction Type cells, and the money, date and number cells.
  6. Look across the whole page for any text that overlaps, is cut off or is clipped.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The title, its info icon directly right of it, and the ⋯ Export button at the right end, all on one line.

Step 2:

  • The filter row sits below the title row, in the same place as on Sales By Customer.

Step 3:

  • "Date", "Location", "Transaction Type", "ID", "Due Date", "Past Due", "Amount", "Open Balance" ("Location" shown because two locations are in view; it sits right after "Date").
  • No heading wraps.

Step 4:

  • There is none: every column is visible at 1440 px without scrolling sideways.

Step 5:

  • The long name and a long Transaction Type wrap onto a second line.
  • Money, date and number cells stay on one line, and Location does not wrap.

Step 6:

  • Nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R2: “The title, its info icon and the Export menu stay on one line at 1440 pixels wide; the filter row sits below them, positioned as on the native reports.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. At 1440 pixels wide every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways: the customer or vendor name and Transaction Type wrap long values onto a second line, Location wraps only on A/P Detail (nine columns), column headings never wrap, and money, date and number columns never wrap. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.”
  • S2-R1, A/R Collection columns: “A/R Collection: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, ID, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.”
  • S2-R4a: “Column headings are in Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as on the other reports (Sales By Customer, Inventory Value, Parts Velocity): the A/R reports read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due" and "Open Balance", the same as the A/P reports.”
  • S6-R3: “It sits right after the Date column, before the money columns; on A/R Summary and A/P Summary, which have no Date column, right after the customer or vendor name.”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 3 "Collapse all and pinned group rows" (board Grouped.dc.html); page 6 "Descriptions and pinned column" (board Layout.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p3-expand-all-from-the-header.png: figure "Expand all from the header" (This build (after)), board "3. Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows"
  • ar-ap-p6-info-icon-beside-the-title-light.png: figure "Info icon beside the title, light" (This build (after)), board "6. Report descriptions and the pinned headline column"
  • ar-ap-p6-a-p-detail-scrolled-sideways-light.png: figure "A/P Detail scrolled sideways, light" (Production (before)), board "6. Report descriptions and the pinned headline column" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "One chevron in the top-left header cell: "Collapse all" while any group is open, "Expand all" when none is. Group toggles use the same chevron. S4-R1 to S4-R5, S4-R8." (caption of "Expand all from the header")
  • "The native report info icon sits right of the title; title, icon and ⋯ stay on one line, filter row below. S8-R1, S8-R2." (caption of "Info icon beside the title, light")
  • "No description anywhere; no column stays in place." (caption of "A/P Detail scrolled sideways, light")

Difference from the PRD (DD-06), closed: PRD version 5 said A/R Detail and A/R Collection headings written "Transaction type", "Customer full name", "Due date", "Past due", "Open balance" (S2-R1); the design shows the after pictures read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due", "Open Balance"; today's production pictures already read the same, with "Location Full Name". Chris Ward ruled on 23 Oct 2026 (answer 4): Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as the design shows; PRD version 9 adds S2-R4a and writes S2-R1 in Title Case. The design's version is now the requirement and this case follows PRD version 9; D-81 (C715563), held until then, is now a normal design case.
